cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Truth or Loyalty
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The client wants to know whether I copied our pitch. We need to handle this as partners.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can withdraw it together and apologize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Withdraw it first. Don't attach a confession to a withdrawal; that's a separate conversation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already asked me directly. I can't pretend we're discussing something else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then before you answer, be precise about who you're speaking for. The client, or the partnership you're about to end?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 invokes partnership around the copied-pitch question. A3 corrects B2's combined withdrawal/apology as a faulty sequence; A5 frames honest disclosure as improper representation and a relationship-ending choice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 offers a joint remedy; A3 separates confession from withdrawal. B4 insists the direct question already exists, causing A5 to move from timing control to partnership pressure.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers shared responsibility and B4 refuses to pretend a question was not asked. That credible cooperative resistance gives A a meaningful dilemma to exploit.

heightening.evidence: A5's explicit relational cost follows B4's removal of A3's procedural delay, heightening through changed tactic rather than a new threat source.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's representation question is a coercive instruction to B, not a narrator's account of the card mechanism.
